annotations.text:
TEN ANIMATIONS, FIVE DEPTHS.

Far: giant floor numerals running down at 139 px/s.
Mid: floor bands with lit windows either side — the parallax that sells height.
Near: speed streaks, staggered so they never pulse in unison.
Foreground: dust motes rising past the camera.
Fastest: the transom slats, read at a glance as speed, on a car that rocks slightly.

The dial now carries a pink arc that fills as the value climbs, the needle sweeps, and the multiplier block pulses.

WHY THIS IS ALLOWED TO GET MORE INTENSE.

There is a hard line here. Intensity tied to THE CRASH TIME is an advance warning and is illegal — there are no warnings before a crash.

Intensity tied to THE MULTIPLIER is only restating a number already on screen. That is the house pattern, intensity(m), and it is what scales these speeds at runtime.

It still sits behind the intensityEffects profile flag, off by default in regulated markets — rising speed and motion are recognised risk factors (checklist D7). The artboard shows the light profile with it on.

Every one of the ten animations stops under prefers-reduced-motion, and the streaks and motes go fully transparent rather than freezing mid-flight. AGENTS.md client conventions.

Still outstanding: the remaining states (betting, collected, the at-or-below-stake return, the cable going, rules), and the compliance gate, which has not run on this concept.
